purpose: Real-account quota E2E evidence: GLM personal (phase 1), GLM team (completed 2026-09-22 from live-provided scope values) and the DeepSeek balance adapter (slice 2), each as HUD extension end-to-end against the live credential plus a same-minute raw read-only API query for cross-checking. The GLM console-side comparison basis is docs/GLM-PLAN-SCOPES.zh-CN.md §6-8 (2026-09-19); DeepSeek is compared against its own raw API response (the balance endpoint is the authoritative source; no separate console screenshot was taken).

environment.host: real Pi TUI (PTY), --no-extensions, model zai-coding-cn/glm-4.7 (GLM personal) / zai-coding-team/glm-5.3 (GLM team) / deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (DeepSeek)
environment.credentialSource: GLM personal: user-level auth.json (zai-coding-cn api_key). GLM team: $ZAI_API_KEY_TEAM env reference in the user's models.json provider, resolved by the host at query time. DeepSeek: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY env var (the auth.json deepseek entry is empty, so the provider's env fallback applies). All resolved by the host; never printed or stored by the HUD
environment.queryEndpoint: GET https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit (GLM personal) / ?type=2 + bigmodel-organization/bigmodel-project (GLM team) / GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance (DeepSeek); all read-only; no model requests

rawSameMinuteQuery.crossCheck: Field mapping verified live: the raw `usage` field is the LIMIT (35000/155000), not used — the adapter correctly maps currentValue→used and takes the server `remaining` verbatim (never re-derived), exactly the §9 synthetic-fixture trap class. Both reset timestamps match to the millisecond. Percentages map exactly (raw percentage 16/80 → HUD 5h 84% / wk 20% remaining). The 58 s gap shows +40 credits consumed in both windows simultaneously (5639→5679, 124038→124078; remaining 29360→29320, 30961→30921) — live consumption counted consistently across the 5h and week pools, not a mapping error. planLabel max = level max. An initial raw attempt that literalized the models.json `$ZAI_API_KEY_TEAM` reference as the key got a business 401 (token expired or incorrect) — operator error before resolution, unrelated to the adapter; the E2E itself never saw a 401.

team.runtimeCoverage: dependency-injected tests additionally cover: host-header scope completion, scope conflict stop, needs-scope refusal, no personal fallback, identity isolation from the personal profile

rawSameMinuteQuery.crossCheck: The HUD row (¥66.90) and the /hud quotas balances match the E2E-time server value exactly: account/granted/topped-up kept as three separate exact-text items, never re-summed, the total being the server's own total_balance. The raw query 32 s later returned 66.85 — a live 0.05 CNY consumption on the account between the two reads, consistent with real-time billing rather than a mapping error; both values are recorded verbatim as sent. is_available=true was returned and (per the adapter contract) intentionally not displayed.

rawSameMinuteQuery.crossCheck: HUD wk 21% is exactly the complement of the server usedPercent 79; resetsAt 1790431051 (unix seconds) maps to the bucket's 2026-09-26T13:57:31.000Z reset; planLabel prolite matches planType; both reads identical within 29 s. The account is the same one Pi's openai-codex OAuth uses (matching accountId prefix observed during research; the HUD itself does not read or verify it — recorded here as research context, not an adapter feature).

protocolFindings: closing stdin immediately after the requests is a shutdown signal: the child exits 0 without answering — the driver keeps stdin open and kills after the answer (found live, covered by a unit test)
the server pushes unsolicited notifications (remoteControl/status/changed) which the reader skips by id matching
a missing node:child_process import in the driver surfaced only at runtime (spawn is not defined) — check.mjs now asserts the import exists alongside the spawn-boundary confinement
